newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strauss says leaning towards Elite buy.
newsitem.headline: Strauss says leaning towards Elite buy.

text.p: The head of the Strauss family said on Monday it was leaning towards exercising an option to buy out its partner's stake in Elite Industries, one of Israel's leading food manufacturers.

Asked if he believed the purchase would go ahead, Michael Strauss told Army Radio: "Yes. I cannot give odds but certainly there is a positive tendency, otherwise we already would have announced a negative decision.
"But there are still two or three things that could cause us to say no."
He was responding to Israeli press reports that the Strauss family, through its Gideon Holdings company, had decided to buy out Elite's biggest shareholder, the Federman group.
"A decision has to be taken soon," Strauss said, referring to a deadline which ends next week for the resolution of a "Buy Me, Buy You" agreement Gideon Holdings has with the Federman group.
Federman has offered to pay Gideon Holdings 38 shekels ($11.14) for every Elite 1 ordinary share it has and 67.25 shekels for every par 5 ordinary share for a total of $66 million.
The terms of the pact between the two feuding partners require Gideon to accept the offer, made in March, or to buy out the Federmans within 60 days at a 2.5 percent discount to the offer price.

The Federman group has a 13 percent equity holding, which gives it voting rights equal to 26.28 percent. The Strauss family, which owns Strauss Dairies, holds at least 17.5 percent of equity and 19.1 percent of voting rights in Elite.
Strauss has said his family and the Federman group had been at loggerheads over running Elite.
Elite has undergone far-reaching changes since the Strauss family came on the scene. Much of the company's loss-making European businesses, acquired in 1992, have been closed or sold off.
